what: Clicking a same-site link makes the current paper (body panel) get cut away from the left while shifting 6% to the right. Along the cut line the paper’s back-side strip (cream gradient·faint shadow) turns over at double speed (squashed to .4x when it overflows the paper width), and a .25 shade clears from the revealed area — cubic ease-in-out curve .8s. The next page rises in .8s (.33,1,.68,1). A page change like turning one leaf of a paperback.

options.push: Share by which the leaving sheet is pushed (ratio of sheet width), default .06
options.stretch: Share the back band stretches after overflowing the paper width, default .4
options.enter: Next section fade-in duration (ms), default 800 — 0 means instant

note: For sites where each page is a separate document — on leaving, a marker is left in sessionStorage and the next document reads it and rises in (leave .8s, then enter .8s, in sequence). The original (Brand) is a single-page app, so the new sheet rises beneath the leaving one during its .8s leave. To reproduce that overlap, you have to fetch the next page and swap only the sheet (see shared.js go() in the original library). Same-page #anchors and new-window links are left alone

from.where: shared.js turnPage — original Nuxt page change onLeave (800ms, push .06 · press .4 · shade .25 · folded line .12) · onEnter (800ms cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1))
